hints: Focus on what Group 2 nitrates always make when heated, think metal oxide plus two gases, not a nitride or NO.
Remember the brown gas is nitrogen dioxide, $\text{NO}_2$, so any equation giving only $\text{NO}$ cannot be right for magnesium.
Now count atoms on each side, you need 2 moles of nitrate to balance Mg, N and O to give 2 MgO, 4 $\text{NO}_2$ and 1 $\text{O}_2$.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Group 2 pattern**

All Group 2 nitrates (except the special case of ammonium) decompose on heating in the same way. You get a metal oxide plus nitrogen dioxide plus oxygen.

General pattern:
$$\text{M}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow \text{MO} + 2\text{NO}_2 + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2$$

**Apply it to magnesium**

For magnesium, the solid product must be magnesium oxide, $\text{MgO}$, and the gases must be $\text{NO}_2$ (brown gas) and $\text{O}_2$. This already rules out equations making $\text{NO}$ or $\text{Mg}_2\text{N}_3$.

Unbalanced idea:
$$\text{Mg}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow \text{MgO} + 2\text{NO}_2 + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2$$

**Balance to whole numbers**

Multiply through by 2 to avoid the half $\text{O}_2$. Check atoms: 2 Mg, 4 N and 12 O on both sides.

Correct balanced equation:
$$2\text{Mg}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

options.A: Unbalanced and chemically wrong. It mixes $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{NO}$ as products. Magnesium nitrate gives only $\text{NO}_2$ plus $\text{O}_2$, never a mixture of nitrogen oxides like this.
options.B: Balanced in atoms but wrong products. It gives $\text{NO}$ instead of $\text{NO}_2$. This is the common confusion between nitrate decomposition (gives $\text{NO}_2$) and other nitrogen chemistry. The brown gas test points to $\text{NO}_2$.
options.C: Exactly right. It follows the Group 2 rule: metal oxide + nitrogen dioxide + oxygen, and it is fully balanced with 2 Mg, 4 N and 12 O on each side.
options.D: Incorrect products and overcomplicated. $\text{Mg}_2\text{N}_3$ is not a correct formula (magnesium nitride is $\text{Mg}_3\text{N}_2$) and nitrides are not formed by heating nitrates in air. Nitrates give oxides, not nitrides.
